tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The show cause notice has been issued to M/s Prudent Corporate Advisory Services Ltd for FY 2021-22 to 2022-23 u/s 74 of the CGST Act, 2017, alleging wrongful availment of input tax credit aggregating to Rs. 3,71,61,875/- in relation to expenses incurred for listing of the company on NSE and BSE through IPO cum OFS, of existing shares. The notice states that transactions relating to issuance of shares under an IPO do not constitute a supply under GST and are not chargeable to tax. On this basis, the department has alleged that the ITC availed on such IPO related expenses is ineligible under Section 16(1) read with Section 17(2) and 17(3) of the CGST Act. Consequently, tax has been proposed to be recovered along with applicable interest under Section 50 and penalty under Section 74(1) read with Section 122.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Goods and Service Tax Department (Gujarat FY 2021-22 & 2022-23)
tax_litigation.status: Matter is pending before Directorate General of Goods & Service Tax Intelligence (DGGI), Zonal Unit, Ahmedabad,Gujarat.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The GST authorities initiated an audit of books of account and records of M/s Prudent Corporate Advisory Services Limited for FY 2022-23 and FY 2023-24 under Section 65 of the CGST Act, 2017, and called for relevant information and supporting documents. Subsequently, A Show cause Notice along with Form GST DRC-01 has been issued to alleging various discrepancies relating to turnover, tax liability and availment of Input Tax Credit (ITC). The key issues include adjustments in turnover reported in GSTR-9C, taxability of income arising from reversal of lease-related provisions, excess availment/utilisation of ITC on B2B supplies, and short reversal of common ITC under Section 17(2) read with Rule 42. It also alleges mismatch of ITC as per books with GSTR-2A and availment of ITC on purchases from a supplier whose GST registration was cancelled. Further, the notice raises issues regarding non-payment/short payment of GST under RCM on legal and other expenses, including fees paid to Independent Directors.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Goods and Service Tax Department (Gujarat FY 2022-23 & 2023-24)
tax_litigation.status: The Company shall furnish its reply within the prescribed timeline.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Income Tax Department has issued a notice under Section 142(1) of the Income-tax Act, 1961 to M/s Prudent Corporate Advisory Services Limited for AY 2025-26,. The notice requires the Company to furnish specified information, documents, reconciliations and explanations in connection with its assessment proceedings. The information sought primarily relates to business and revenue streams, trade payables and commission payouts, TDS compliance, CSR expenditure, depreciation on customer folios/intangible assets, investments and capital gains, Schedule BP adjustments, GST/AIS reconciliations, deduction under Section 80JJAA, fixed assets and related-party payments. The notice is information-seeking in nature and does not itself quantify any tax demand, penalty or addition/disallowance.
tax_litigation.status: The reply to the said notice has been submitted and the matter is presently pending consideration before the Assessing officer, Assessment Unit, Income Tax Department.
